name: Orvana Geneware Executive Presence Suit
description:
A Tier 5 bespoke suit designed for the growing population of Spire executives who have undergone significant geneware modification and refuse to let it diminish their sartorial authority. The jacket is a fluid-structured double-breasted cut by Orvana's atelier division, executed in 'luminwave silk-wool' — a fabric that shifts between a warm charcoal and a deep amber-bronze depending on the angle of light, achieved through a nano-fiber orientation process that takes roughly four hours per panel to set. The rear of the jacket is cut in an asymmetric drape rather than a standard back panel, opening into a wide, structured wing-slit: two reinforced channels of matching luminwave fabric that frame non-functional decorative wings or small functional geneware wing structures without compressing the membrane. The slit edges are finished with a thin line of brushed gold-alloy trim that catches light at the perimeter of any wing display. The tail accommodation is built into the trouser: a high-waisted wide-leg pant in matching luminwave with a rear pleat system that opens into a clean, fully finished tail-vent, the opening framed in the same gold-alloy trim as the jacket wing-slit, creating a deliberate visual continuity between the geneware accommodations as design elements rather than afterthoughts.

The shirt beneath is an Orvana Silk-Analog Drape Blouse in deep ivory with a draped open collar that sits wide at the sternum, accommodating any bioluminescent skin modifications at the chest and throat without coverage that would obscure them. Footwear is the Caelum IX Pressure-Form Dress Heel in matte black with a gold-alloy cap-toe, adding height without instability. The BCI neural port at the base of the skull is framed by the jacket's collar, which has been cut with a precise oval relief that exposes the port as an intentional detail — a polished chrome ring trim around the opening making it look like a piece of architectural hardware. This outfit does not hide what the wearer is. It builds a room around it.
functionality: Wing-slit rear jacket channels with reinforced structural framing for geneware wing accommodation. Tail-vent trouser pleat system with full finish for biological tail modifications. Neural port oval relief in collar with decorative chrome ring surround. Bioluminescence-exposing open drape collar on blouse. Luminwave fabric shifts color in ambient light, providing passive visual presence enhancement. Pressure-form heel provides stability correction for modified lower-body proportions.
what_it_says: Power and transformation, combined without apology. This wearer has ascended to Tier 5 and has also chosen to modify their body, and they have commissioned an outfit that treats both facts as equally worthy of celebration. The gold-alloy trim on the wing-slit and tail-vent says: this was designed for me, not adapted for me. The luminwave color shift says: I occupy different space depending on where you're standing.
worn_by: Spire-resident corponation board members with wing or tail modifications
senior TESSERA Genomics executives who wear their own work
old-money Spire families who adopted geneware as a generational statement
manufacturer: Orvana Atelier (bespoke Tier 5 geneware-forward fashion house)
price_range: Φ 65,000–Φ 200,000+ (bespoke commission, geneware scan required prior to fitting)
story_hooks: A Tier 3 worker assigned to deliver documents to a Spire boardroom sees this outfit for the first time and later describes it in obsessive detail to someone who has never been above Tier 2 — the description becomes a kind of legend, details mutating with each retelling.

The luminwave fabric's nano-fiber orientation begins degrading under a specific frequency of security scanner — the suit starts flickering between its color states in a high-security checkpoint, drawing exactly the kind of attention a Tier 5 executive cannot afford in that particular building.

A rival executive commissions a counterfeit version of this outfit from a street-label tailor — the wing-slit channels are slightly wrong, the tail-vent doesn't drape correctly, and the original wearer notices immediately at a cross-corponation summit, turning a fashion observation into a negotiating advantage.

physical_description.visual_profile: A commanding, angular silhouette that celebrates rather than conceals geneware modification. The asymmetric wing-slit jacket creates a dramatic vertical emphasis, while the high-waisted trousers elongate the figure. The overall impression is neo-corporate formality merged with body-modification pride—a statement that augmentation is power, not shame.
physical_description.fit: Precision tailored through the shoulder and chest, with a structured double-breasted closure. The jacket drapes fluidly but maintains architectural sharpness. Trousers are high-waisted and wide-leg, allowing freedom of movement and accommodation for functional geneware without constraint.
physical_description.primary_material: Luminwave silk-wool (nano-fiber treated, angle-responsive), matching the trousers. The blouse is silk-analog in ivory. Brushed gold-alloy trim throughout. Matte black pressure-form leather on heels with gold-alloy cap-toe.
physical_description.texture: The luminwave fabric has a subtle iridescence—smooth and lustrous to the touch, with depth that shifts under movement. The silk-analog drape blouse is fluid and soft. Gold trim is tactile, slightly warm. Pressure-form heels are sleek and seamless.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: warm charcoal-to-amber-bronze luminwave (angle-dependent). Secondary: deep ivory blouse. Accent: brushed gold-alloy hardware on trim, cap-toe, and BCI port frame. Matte black heels ground the palette.
physical_description.closures: Double-breasted magnetic snap system on jacket (silent, retrofittable). Friction-fit trousers with integrated tail-vent pleats. Heels are pressure-form fitted.
distinctive_features: Asymmetric wing-slit jacket rear with reinforced channels for functional/decorative geneware wings
Gold-alloy trim framing wing-slit edges and matching tail-vent opening
High-waisted trousers with rear pleat system and finished tail-vent
BCI neural port deliberately exposed at nape with polished chrome architectural framing
Open-collar silk-analog blouse exposing bioluminescent chest/throat modifications
Luminwave fabric nano-fiber treatment creating dynamic light-response
Caelum IX heels with gold-alloy cap-toe detailing
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 bespoke luxury masquerading as Tier 1 corpo formality. The price point and hand-labor indicate ultra-high-end, but the deliberate geneware accommodation suggests Spire-adjacent elite who have rejected corpo conformity in favor of modified authenticity.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Spire executives, geneware pioneers, and those who have undergone significant biomod and want to wear it as armor, not apology. Signals confidence in augmentation, wealth enough for bespoke tailoring, and rejection of the old corpo aesthetic that demanded hiding modifications. A statement piece for the post-human executive class.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; worn pieces show a subtle patina on gold trim and fabric lustre from movement. The luminwave fabric only improves with age as the nano-fibers settle into deeper light-response. No visible wear intended—this is investment-grade.

image_prompt: A statuesque androgynous figure in a tailored Orvana bespoke suit stands in three-quarter profile against a dark Spire interior backdrop. The luminwave silk-wool jacket shifts from charcoal to warm bronze under moody gallery lighting, the asymmetric rear wing-slit open and framed by brushed gold trim. Functional bio-luminescent wings or chrome-edged wing extensions visible through the slit, catching rim light. High-waisted trousers match the jacket, with the tail-vent finished in matching gold-alloy trim. The deep ivory drape blouse beneath sits open at the collarbone, exposing bioluminescent skin modifications at the throat. The BCI neural port at the nape is deliberately visible, framed in polished chrome that catches light like architectural hardware. Matte black Caelum IX heels with gold cap-toe complete the look. Moody, dramatic lighting emphasizes the iridescent shift of the luminwave fabric and the intentional exposure of geneware. Neo-noir luxury, post-human confidence. --ar 2:3 --v 6
